interpretation: The identical claim registers a different separation cost as the receiver's prior context density changes (junior vs. senior researcher), and at every density the registration is a correct, floor-attaining individuation in that receiver's own graph. No single density's registration is privileged; a global, receiver-independent relevance score would have to pick one and be wrong for every other receiver.
theorem: Theorem 4.4 (Distinct Receivers Register Distinct, Equally Correct Cells)
